cases.question: How far may a worker be from a means of exit inside a trench?
cases.answer: A means of exit should be provided from the inside of the trench, usually no more than 8m (25 ft) away than any worker in the trench [Page 103].

cases.question: What are the tube-and-coupler scaffold mid rail, top rail and toe board dimensions?
cases.answer:  The mid rail and Top rail shall be at height 600 mm and 1200 mm respectively and toe boards (150mm) shall be securely attached to the platform. [Page 78]

cases.question: Which Indian Standard covers the code of safety for excavation work?
cases.answer: IS 3764, 1992 Code of safety for excavation work [Page 206]

cases.question: What is the maximum allowable slope for excavations in Type B soil?
cases.answer: Type B:  All simple slope excavations 20 feet (6Mt) or less in depth will have a maximum allowable slope of 1:1.  All benched excavations 20 feet (6Mt) or less in depth will have a maximum allowable slope of 1:1 and maximum bench dimensions as indicated.  All excavations 20 feet (6Mt) or less in depth which have vertically sided lower portions will be shielded or supported to a height at least 18 inches (0.5Mt) above the top of the vertical side. All such excavations will have a maximum allowable slope of 1:1. [Page 105]

cases.question: What about Type C soil?
cases.answer: Type C:  All simple slope excavations 20 feet (6Mt) or less in depth will have a maximum allowable slope of 1 1/2:1.  All excavations 20 feet (6Mt) or less in depth which have vertically sided lower portions will be shielded or supported to a height at least 18 inches above the top of the vertical side. All such excavations will have a maximum allowable slope of 1 1/2:1. [Page 105]

cases.question: What are the five basic steps of HIRA?
cases.answer:
I. Initiating the HIRA [Page 25]
II. Identify the hazard [Page 25]
III. Identify all parties affected by the hazard and determine how they can be affected [Page 25]
IV. Evaluate or assess the risk [Page 25]
V. Monitor & Review [Page 25]

cases.question: What makes a space a confined space?
cases.answer:
A confined space is a space that has any of the following defining features:
* In which a person can bodily enter [Page 97].
* Contains material that has the potential to engulf an entrant [Page 97].
* Contains or has a potential to contain a hazardous atmosphere [Page 97].
* Has walls that converge inward such that the entrant could be trapped [Page 97].
* Which has limited entry / egress [Page 97].
* Which is not meant for occupancy [Page 97].
Generally, it is a place which is substantially (though not always entirely) enclosed with a reasonably foreseeable risk of serious injury from hazardous substances or conditions within the space or nearby [Page 97].

cases.question: What is a trench?
cases.answer: A trench is an excavation in which the depth exceeds (is bigger than) the width. [Page 102]

cases.question: Summarize Chapter 13 Excavation.
cases.answer:
* An excavation is a hole in the ground resulting from removing material [Page 102].
* A trench is an excavation where the depth is greater than the width [Page 102].
* Soil type(s) related to the excavation or trench must be identified [Page 102].
* Protective system design considers soil classification, depth of cut, water content of soil, weather and climate, and other operations in the vicinity [Page 104].
* The employer or supervisor is responsible for identifying all hazards and risks before starting work [Page 102].
* Excavated material and pipes must be placed 1 metre away from the edge of the excavation or trench wall [Page 107].

cases.question: In the risk assessment matrix, what is the description and control level for a relative risk rating between 21 and 25?
cases.answer: 21-25 — Risk requires an immediate attention; action must be documented and completion time limit may be decided. — Very high [Page 29]

cases.question: When must employers provide PPE to workers?
cases.answer: Employers must provide personal protective equipment (PPE) to their employees when engineering or work practice controls are not feasible or do not provide sufficient protection [Page 163]. This is necessary when controlling a hazard at its source is the best way to protect employees [Page 163].

cases.question: What pressure can high-pressure gas cylinders withstand?
cases.answer: High-pressure cylinders can withstand up to 10000 psi [Page 152].

cases.question: What minimum load must a scaffold be able to support?
cases.answer:  Scaffolds shall be designed to support at least 4 times the anticipated weight of Men and material [Page 78]

cases.question: At what trench depth is a protective system generally required?
cases.answer: In general, trenches that are 1.2 metres (4 feet) deep or greater require a protective system unless the excavation is made entirely in stable rock. [Page 103]

cases.question: What are the four elements of fire?
cases.answer: Fire is defined by the four elements which are Fuel, Energy, and Oxygen, and chain reaction [Page 175]. Earlier fire was represented by the fire triangle with three elements: oxygen, heat, and fuel [Page 175]. A fourth element plays a vital role in the existence and spread of fire, which is the chain reaction [Page 175].

cases.question: What emergencies must a construction-site emergency plan consider?
cases.answer:
A. Serious injuries or Poisoning [Page 196]
B. Fire or Explosion, [Page 196]
C. Chemical leak or spill, [Page 196]
D. Electrocution, [Page 196]
E. Structural collapse. [Page 196]
F. Flood or Earthquake [Page 196]

cases.question: What must be done before moving a mobile scaffold?
cases.answer:
* Remove all material and equipment from the platform before moving scaffolding [Page 79].
* Do not try to move rolling scaffolding without sufficient help [Page 79].
* Watch out for holes in the floor and for overhead obstructions [Page 79].
* Do not use brackets on rolling scaffoldings without first considering the overturning effect [Page 79].

cases.question: In the likelihood table, what rating is given to a Possible occurrence?
cases.answer: Possible — Chances of occurring but not unusual — 4 [Page 28]

cases.question: In the severity table, what rating is assigned to a Fatal hazard?
cases.answer: Fatal — One fatality, property damage — 4 [Page 28]

cases.question: In the relative risk table, what control level applies to a risk value of 13-20?
cases.answer: 13-20 — Risk requires an attention; action may be followed up and completion time limit may be decided. — High [Page 29]
